text:
Jon Miller: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I'm seeing a small but consistent bump in queue-wait P95 for long-context routes (seq>2048). probed a few hosts, looks like more time waiting for kernel handoff than actual execution.
Maya Gupta: can you paste the per-route p95s? is this only on dedicated or also hosted? :thinking_face:
Jon Miller: mostly dedicated pools, but a couple hosted routes show the pattern. rough numbers: routeA p95 queue_wait 92ms -> 140ms, routeB 48ms -> 70ms. CPU/gpu utilization unchanged.
Liam O'Connor: hmm could be the kernel scoring threshold change causing more cross-kernel rebinds. do we have histograms of batch sizes + handoff counts?
Jon Miller: I pulled the sampler logs and a small snippet of kernel-handoff events per request. attaching inline excerpt: ```handoff_count, avg_batch_at_handoff
1, 8
2, 12
1, 9
3, 5
```
Maya Gupta: cool. two quick asks: (1) add a token-level latency breakdown (queue vs kernel vs kv_read) for these routes, (2) record a batch-size histogram keyed by kernel_variant so we can see if certain kernels attract smaller batches.
perf-bot: snapshot uploaded — https://perf.redwood/internal/snapshots/1765432100/queue-kernel-compare :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sara Li: also worth adding scheduler_efficiency = useful_tokens / (tokens_reserved) metric and a simple alert if efficiency < 0.65 for 5m on these pools. low-efficiency correlates with cost regressions.
Liam O'Connor: agreed. for instrumentation I propose a PromQL gauge: ```sum by(route,kernel) (rate(batch_size_bucket_count[5m])) / sum by(route,kernel) (rate(request_count[5m]))``` as a quick proxy for avg batch size per kernel.
Maya Gupta: +1. and token-level breakdown could be a stacked waterfall in the dashboard: queue_wait, kv_hit/kv_miss, kernel_exec, postproc. we can sample 1% of requests to export full per-token traces to avoid noise.
Jon Miller: i'll add the sampling patch and a lightweight label on requests: sample_trace=true. will also emit kernel_variant on the batch metric.
Sara Li: once that's in, can you run a 30m smoke with the old selector vs new one on a canary pool? then we'll compare the waterfall and batch histograms.
Jon Miller: yes — scheduling a canary now. rough plan: 10k requests per variant, collect histograms, post results back here.
Maya Gupta: thanks — if the regression maps to smaller batches on the new selector we should consider a hysteresis rule: prefer current kernel if expected batch_size < threshold to avoid frequent handoffs.
Liam O'Connor: also add kvcache metrics: kv_lookup_time and kv_eviction_count per route — misses amplify kernel work.
Jon Miller: noted. i'll update the PR with metrics + dashboard draft and ping infra for canary run.
perf-bot: canary job queued (job_id=canary-1765432100). updates will appear here.
Sara Li: :thumbsup: keep it short and measurable. if we see efficiency drop, we'll rollback selector tweak.
Jon Miller: will do — thanks everyone.
